title: AI_washing
summary:
AI washing is a deceptive marketing tactic that consists of promoting a product or a service by overstating the role of artificial intelligence and the integration of it. Companies often engage in the practice to mislead customers to boost their offerings, and to secure funding from investors. The term is derived from greenwashing, another deceptive marketing technique that involves environmental impact in a similar guise. The term "AI washing" was first coined in 2019 by the AI Now Institute, a research institute based at New York University.

AI washing might involve a company claiming to have used AI in the development or enhancement of its products or services without its actual involvement, or using buzzwords such as "smart" or "AI-powered" without the product actually offering it or making use of it. AI washing has been compared to the dot-com bubble, when businesses appended "dot-com" to the end of the business name to boost their valuation.

Notable examples include Coca-Cola releasing Coca-Cola Y3000 in September 2023, claiming the flavor had been "co-created with human and artificial intelligence" with no proof of AI involvement; Amazon's AI-powered Just Walk Out technology in Amazon Fresh grocery stores, which was scrutinized when reports circulated that the company employs more than 1,000 employees to manually check more than 75% of the transactions; and in March 2024, the SEC charging two investment advisers with making false and misleading statements about their use of artificial intelligence, with the firms agreeing to pay $400,000 in civil penalties.

Gary Gensler, Chair of the Securities and Exchange Commission, warned in a February 2024 speech at Yale University that some companies were engaging in AI washing, which can break U.S. securities law, mislead consumers and harm investors. The Federal Trade Commission recently announced five cases exposing AI-related deception as part of Operation AI Comply, a law enforcement sweep focused on companies using AI to deceive or harm consumers. AI washing poses significant challenges for consumers, businesses and the broader AI industry, and can damage a company's reputation and erode customer loyalty.
